add-remove.title: Add/Remove
add-remove.description: Dynamically add and remove elements from the page
add-remove.information: As well as being able to dynamically add and remove elements from the page, you can also add `?initialElements=X` onto the url to generate elements on load.

autocomplete.title: Autocomplete
autocomplete.description: Pick a value from suggestions that appear as you type.
autocomplete.information: Start typing in either box to see suggestions. Use the up and down arrow keys to move through them (they wrap round), Enter to choose the highlighted one, or click a suggestion; Escape closes the list and a second Escape clears the box. Tabbing away closes the list without choosing anything, and changing the text after choosing clears the choice. The input follows the ARIA combobox pattern: aria-expanded says whether the list is open and aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted option, which has aria-selected="true". Suggestions match anywhere in a name, ignoring case and accents, with names that start with what you typed listed first, and the matching part is in bold. The country box filters a fixed list straight away. The city box asks a slow pretend server instead: it waits for at least {{min}} characters and a {{debounce}}ms pause in typing, shows a loading message while it waits, returns at most {{max}} cities, and answers short searches more slowly than long ones, so an old answer can arrive after a new one; only the answer for the current text is shown.

check-box.title: Checkbox
check-box.description: A set of checkbox scenarios to test against.

drag-and-drop.title: Drag and Drop
drag-and-drop.description: Drag elements from one side of the page and drop them on the other side.
drag-and-drop.information: You able to drag an infinite amount of the red boxes and drop them on the grey box.

drag-and-drop-hard.title: Drag and Drop (Hard)
drag-and-drop-hard.description: Drag the appropriate smaller shapes onto the larger shape.
drag-and-drop-hard.information: A correct drop will result in the shape turning green, otherwise the shape will turn yellow. Note: the shapes change on each reload

dropdown.title: Dropdown
dropdown.description: Pick options from a native select, a multi-select and a custom dropdown.
dropdown.information: There are three kinds of dropdown here. The first two are native <select> elements, so most frameworks can choose an option directly by its value or text; the second allows several options to be picked at once. The third is a custom dropdown built from buttons and a list: it is not a <select>, and its options only exist in the DOM, at the end of the page, while it is open, so click it to open it and then click an option. Some options are disabled and cannot be picked. Your current choices are shown underneath.

dynamic-table.information: Note: the table data refreshes on a reload.

file-upload.information: The upload can be anywhere between 1-10 seconds regardless of size as the upload function is mocked.

form-validation.description: A registration form whose inputs are validated, so you can check the error messages shown for incorrectly formatted values.
form-validation.information: Errors appear when you leave a field and when you submit the form. Phone and website are optional but must be valid if filled in. Age must be a whole number between 18 and 120. The password needs at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a number.

geolocation.title: Geolocation
geolocation.description: Find the browser's location, then follow it as it moves.
geolocation.information: The browser asks for permission before sharing its location, and that prompt is not part of the page, so grant (or deny) the geolocation permission and set a fake location in your test framework before clicking. "Get my location" reads the position once; "Start watching" keeps following it, so change the fake location and the page will update. The coordinates, their accuracy and the nearest of a few well known cities are shown underneath. If permission is denied, the position cannot be found or it takes too long, an error explains why.

hovers.title: Hovers
hovers.description: Interact with elements that only appear while the mouse is over something.
hovers.information: Everything on this page only shows up while the mouse pointer rests on something, so tests have to hover first. The details on each profile card are not in the DOM at all until the card is hovered, and on purpose there is no other way to reveal them. The buttons on each file are always in the DOM but stay invisible until their row is hovered, so a test that clicks them straight away will be told they are not visible; keyboard users can also reveal them by tabbing to the row. The menu opens its submenus a moment after an item is hovered and closes a moment after the pointer leaves it, so move through it the way a person would; clicking an item opens its submenu straight away. The last thing you did is shown underneath.

files.title: Files

iframes.title: IFrames
iframes.description: Forms, nested frames and a rich text editor that live inside iframes, so you have to switch into a frame to reach them.
iframes.information: Everything inside an iframe belongs to a separate document, so selectors run on the page cannot find it: tests have to switch into the frame first, and back out again to check anything on the page. The form sends its message to the page outside the frame. The counter sits inside a frame that is itself inside another frame, so it takes two switches to reach. The rich text editor works like many classic WYSIWYG editors: the text you edit is the body of a frame, while its toolbar, word count and HTML output are on the page around it, so a test has to move between the two.

infinite-scroll.title: Infinite Scroll
infinite-scroll.description: A list that keeps loading new items every time you reach the bottom of the page.
infinite-scroll.information: Scroll to the end of the list to load the next batch of 10 items. A loading indicator is shown for a moment before the new items appear, and the feed never runs out, so wait for the new items rather than for the end of the list.
infinite-scroll.item-description: This is the content of item {{number}}. Keep scrolling to load more.

js-alerts.title: JS Alerts
js-alerts.description: Handle the browser's native alert, confirm and prompt dialogs, which are not part of the page.
js-alerts.information: Each button opens one of the browser's built-in JavaScript dialogs. They are drawn by the browser rather than the page, so they cannot be found in the DOM: listen for the dialog, check its message, then accept or dismiss it (typing an answer into the prompt first). The result of your choice is shown on the page once the dialog closes.

key-presses.title: Key Presses
key-presses.description: Interact with the page by pressing keys on the keyboard.
key-presses.information: Everything on this page is driven by the keyboard, so tests have to send key presses rather than click or type text. The key reader shows the last key pressed in its text box, with its key and code and any modifier keys held with it, plus the last few keys pressed. The counter only changes while it has focus: the up and down (or right and left) arrow keys move it by 1, holding Shift moves it by 10, Home and End jump to the lowest and highest values and Escape puts it back where it started. The hold control only confirms if Space is held down for a whole second; letting go sooner does not count, and holding a key down repeats its keydown event, so each repeat has to be ignored. There is no mouse alternative on purpose.

reader.label: Press any key in this box

counter.label: Counter
counter.instructions: Focus the counter, then use the arrow keys to change it. Hold Shift to move in steps of 10. Home and End jump to 0 and 100, and Escape resets it to 50.

hold.instructions: Focus the box below and hold Space down for {{seconds}} second to confirm.

multiple-windows.title: Multiple Windows
multiple-windows.description: Links and buttons that open new tabs and popup windows, which tests have to switch to and back from.
multiple-windows.information: Every tab or window has a document of its own, so a test only sees the one it is focused on: it has to wait for the new window, switch to it, and switch back to the original afterwards. Each window sets its own document title to tell it apart. The popup sends a message back to the window that opened it, then closes itself, while the page keeps track of whether it is still open. The two named-window links both open in the same window, so clicking the second reuses it instead of opening another.

shadow-dom.title: Shadow DOM
shadow-dom.description: Elements hidden inside open, nested and closed shadow roots, so you can check how your tools reach into the shadow DOM.
shadow-dom.information: Regular selectors stop at a shadow root boundary. The open shadow root can be pierced by most tools, the nested example needs two hops, the slotted content lives in the light DOM even though it is shown inside a shadow root, and the closed shadow root cannot be reached through host.shadowRoot at all.

sortable-table.title: Sortable Table
sortable-table.description: Sort a table by clicking its column headers.
sortable-table.information: Click a column header to sort by it: the first click sorts ascending, the second descending and the third puts the rows back in their original order. The sorted column's header says which way it is sorted in its aria-sort attribute, and the other headers have none; the Email column cannot be sorted. The values are picked to catch naive sorting: salaries and project counts sort wrongly as text, start dates are shown in your language's format, one name starts with an accented letter, and several people share a department (they keep their original order when tied). The contractor has no salary and always sorts last, whichever way the column is sorted. The current sort is shown underneath the table.
